file.content:
name: test

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Release evidence is proved on the tag you actually ship from. Before
    # this, the repo had NO release-time evidence check at all: the gate ran
    # only on pushes to main, so a tag could be cut without its proof ever
    # being verified at the point it is published.
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  # So anyone can ask "is the evidence release-ready?" without cutting a tag.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - run: go vet ./...
      - name: Test browser controller request lifetimes
        run: node --test webui/tests/*.test.cjs
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with: { python-version: "3.14" }
      - run: python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.1
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/coverage -p 'test_*.py'
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/release-hygiene -p 'test_*.py'
      # The adapters are only meaningful against the frameworks they adapt, so
      # CI installs them. Without them the suite still runs and skips those
      # cases, which would quietly assert nothing.
      - run: python3 -m pip install langchain-core==1.6.4 llama-index-core==0.14.25
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s sdk/python/tests -p 'test_*.py'
      - run: |
          unformatted=$(gofmt -l -s .)
          if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
            echo "::error::unformatted files:"
            echo "$unformatted"
            exit 1
          fi

  browser-smoke:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with: { node-version: "22" }
      - run: npm ci --prefix webui --ignore-scripts
      - run: npm exec --prefix webui -- playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-brain" ./cmd/entire-brain
      - name: Exercise the embedded UI in Chromium
        run: BRAIN_VIZ_BINARY="$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-brain" npm --prefix webui run test:browser
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: browser-smoke-traces
          path: webui/test-results/

  regression-mutations:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - name: Prove the selected tests catch their intended regressions
        run: python3 -B tools/coverage/mutation_check.py

  build:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    strategy:
      matrix:
        goos: [darwin, linux, windows]
        goarch: [amd64, arm64]
        exclude:
          - { goos: windows, goarch: arm64 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - env:
          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
        run: go build ./...

  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            runner: depot-ubuntu-24.04-8
          - os: macos-latest
            runner: depot-macos-26
    # The explicit name keeps matrix.runner out of the default display name:
    # "test (<os>)" is a required check on main.
    name: test (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Backstop only. go test -timeout fires first and prints which tests were
    # still running, which is the useful artefact; neither job had any cap, so
    # a genuine hang ran to GitHub's 360-minute default.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - name: Test with coverage and binary contracts
        run: python3 -B tools/coverage/run.py --race --output "${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage"
      - name: Retain coverage and test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-default-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.jsonl
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.out
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.html

  windows-test-prepare:
    name: test (windows-latest) / compile and plan
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-8
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      shard-matrix: ${{ steps.shard-matrix.outputs.value }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Validate the Windows sharding harness
        run: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p "test_*.py" -v
      - name: Compile once and inventory default-runnable roots
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $repository = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.').Path
          $output = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'windows-test-bundle'
          & python -B tools/ci-bench/windows-production/prepare.py `
            --repository $repository `
            --output $output `
            --settings tools/ci-bench/windows-production/settings.json `
            --weights tools/ci-bench/windows-production/historical-weights.json `
            --expected-repository-sha '${{ github.sha }}'
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
      - name: Export the authoritative shard matrix
        id: shard-matrix
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $planPath = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'windows-test-bundle/plan.json'
          $plan = Get-Content -LiteralPath $planPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          $indexes = @($plan.shards | ForEach-Object { [int] $_.index })
          if ($indexes.Count -ne [int] $plan.shardCount -or $indexes.Count -eq 0) {
            throw 'plan shard indexes do not match shardCount'
          }
          $matrix = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $indexes -Compress
          "value=$matrix" | Out-File -LiteralPath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Encoding utf8 -Append
      - name: Upload immutable Windows test bundle
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: windows-test-bundle
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle
          if-no-files-found: error
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 3

  windows-test-shards:
    name: test (windows-latest) / shard ${{ matrix.shard }}
    needs: windows-test-prepare
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-4
    timeout-minutes: 35
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 8
      matrix:
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(needs.windows-test-prepare.outputs.shard-matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: windows-test-bundle
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle
      - name: Execute the assigned compiled roots
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $repository = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.').Path
          $bundle = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle').Path
          $output = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'windows-test-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}'
          & python -B tools/ci-bench/windows-production/run_shard.py `
            --repository $repository `
            --bundle $bundle `
            --output $output `
            --shard-index '${{ matrix.shard }}' `
            --expected-repository-sha '${{ github.sha }}'
          exit $LASTEXITCODE
      - name: Upload shard evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: windows-test-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  windows-test-other:
    name: test (windows-latest) / non-heavy packages
    needs: windows-test-prepare
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-4
    timeout-minutes: 40
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: windows-test-bundle
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle
      - name: Run every target-Windows non-heavy package once
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $repository = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.').Path
          $bundle = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle').Path
          $output = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'windows-test-other'
          & python -B tools/ci-bench/windows-production/run_other.py `
            --repository $repository `
            --bundle $bundle `
            --output $output `
            --expected-repository-sha '${{ github.sha }}'
          exit $LASTEXITCODE
      - name: Measure instrumented CLI contracts without rerunning the suite
        run: python -B tools/coverage/run.py --race --binary-only --output "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-other/binary-coverage"
      - name: Upload non-heavy package evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: windows-test-other
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-other
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  windows-test-vet:
    name: test (windows-latest) / vet
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-4
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
      - run: go vet -race ./...

  windows-test-verify:
    name: test (windows-latest) / coverage and integrity
    needs: [windows-test-prepare, windows-test-shards, windows-test-other]
    if: ${{ always() && needs.windows-test-prepare.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: windows-test-bundle
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: windows-test-shard-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: windows-test-other
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-other
      - name: Verify exact root, package, process, and artifact coverage
        run: |
          python -B tools/ci-bench/windows-production/verify_results.py \
            --bundle "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-bundle" \
            --shard-results "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-shards" \
            --other-results "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-other" \
            --coverage-output "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-statement-coverage" \
            --output "${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-verification.json"
      - name: Render merged Windows statement coverage
        run: go tool cover -html="${{ runner.temp }}/windows-statement-coverage/combined.out" -o="${{ runner.temp }}/windows-statement-coverage/coverage.html"
      - name: Upload Windows statement coverage
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-windows-sharded
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-statement-coverage/
          if-no-files-found: warn
      - name: Upload verification report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: windows-test-verification
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/windows-test-verification.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  # Keep the former matrix check identity stable for required-check migration.
  windows-test:
    name: test (windows-latest)
    needs:
      [windows-test-prepare, windows-test-shards, windows-test-other, windows-test-vet, windows-test-verify]
    if: always()
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    steps:
      - name: Require every Windows test component
        env:
          PREPARE_RESULT: ${{ needs.windows-test-prepare.result }}
          SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.windows-test-shards.result }}
          OTHER_RESULT: ${{ needs.windows-test-other.result }}
          VET_RESULT: ${{ needs.windows-test-vet.result }}
          VERIFY_RESULT: ${{ needs.windows-test-verify.result }}
        run: |
          for result in "$PREPARE_RESULT" "$SHARDS_RESULT" "$OTHER_RESULT" "$VET_RESULT" "$VERIFY_RESULT"; do
            if [ "$result" != success ]; then
              echo "A required Windows test component ended with: $result" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

  phase1-semantic:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            runner: depot-ubuntu-24.04-8
          - os: macos-latest
            runner: depot-macos-26
          - os: windows-latest
            runner: depot-windows-2025-8
    name: phase1-semantic (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    env:
      ENTIRE_BRAIN_PHASE1_CI: "1"
      GOPROXY: "off"
      GOSUMDB: "off"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - name: Prime module cache
        env:
          GOPROXY: "https://proxy.golang.org,direct"
          GOSUMDB: "sum.golang.org"
        run: go mod download
      - name: Run deterministic Phase 1 semantic tests
        run: go test -race -timeout 20m ./internal/cli -run 'TestPhase1|TestSemantic|TestWorkspace|TestMCP|TestRefreshSemantic'

  # Discover every Python benchmark test module; Go tests do not cover the harness.
  benchmark-corpus:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    steps:
      # fetch-depth 0: the packet-format A/B modules assert that a recorded
      # product-contract commit is an ancestor of HEAD, which a depth-1 checkout
      # cannot answer.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      # Evidence packaging uses tarfile's zstd support from Python 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with: { python-version: "3.14" }
      # The task negative-control module drives the pinned Go toolchain. Same
      # story: the job had no Go at all.
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.26.2" }
      # That module discovers its toolchain with GOPROXY=off, deliberately — the
      # receipt it produces is only a negative control if the runtime is fixed
      # and local. So the pin it names has to be in the module cache before it
      # runs; this is the one command allowed to fetch it.
      - name: Prime the Go toolchain the task negative control pins
        run: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.4 go version
      - name: Install Python coverage tracer
        run: python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.1
      - name: Validate mined-scale corpus and run the benchmark test suite
        run: |
          set -e
          python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/mined-scale/check_manifest.py
          python3 -B -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/memory-ladder -p 'test_*.py'
          python3 -B tools/coverage/python_run.py --output "${{ runner.temp }}/python-coverage"
      - name: Retain Python coverage and module outcomes
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-python-benchmarks
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/python-coverage/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/python-coverage/*.log
            ${{ runner.temp }}/python-coverage/html/

  release-evidence:
    # Release-evidence audits enforce proof-ready release artifacts: they prove
    # a retained performance or tool claim was measured against the code being
    # shipped. That question is asked AT RELEASE, which is where this now runs
    # — on a v* tag, or on demand via workflow_dispatch.
    #
    # It used to run on every push to main, and that was the wrong trigger. The
    # manifests pin six source files by content hash, including test files, so
    # ANY edit to them marks the measurement stale — the run that made main red
    # on 2026-09-11 was tripped by `style(distill): group fact merge imports
    # consistently`, an import-grouping change that cannot affect a scheduler
    # benchmark. The evidence has been re-recorded eight times since June for
    # this reason, and went stale again six days after the last re-record
    # (#194). A gate that red-lights main for reasons unrelated to the commit
    # being pushed does not enforce anything; it teaches everyone to ignore CI,
    # and the one failure that matters goes with it.
    #
    # NOTHING IS WEAKENED. The audits still run with --fail-on-flags and still
    # refuse a stale report; a tag carrying stale evidence fails exactly as it
    # would have. What changed is that ordinary development on main no longer
    # trips a release-time proof, and a release can no longer be cut without
    # that proof being checked.
    #
    # Re-record before tagging: regenerate the retained artifacts on a
    # representative machine (the timings are hardware-specific), then commit
    # the manifest and both report files together.
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    # Deliberately GitHub-hosted: the release path keeps working during a
    # Depot outage.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Check retained release evidence
        run: |
          # Every lane is checked before the job decides. `set -e` used to stop at
          # the first failing audit, so a red main reported one stale lane while
          # hiding the rest: on 2026-08-19 two lanes went stale in the same merge,
          # only the Radar tool lane was ever named, and the change that refreshed
          # it would have left main red on the distill lane nobody had seen.
          set -uo pipefail
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          failures=0
          check() {
            label="$1"
            shift
            if ! "$@"; then
              echo "::error::release-evidence check failed: $label"
              failures=$((failures + 1))
            fi
          }
          compare() {
            label="$1"
            committed="$2"
            generated="$3"
            if ! cmp -s "$committed" "$generated"; then
              echo "::error::retained $label report is stale: $(basename "$committed")"
              diff -u "$committed" "$generated" >&2 || true
              failures=$((failures + 1))
            fi
          }
          check "benchmark harness tests" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/run_test.py
          check "replay-lab release evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_codex.py \
            --results benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release \
            --release-manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "clean replay-lab proof" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_codex.py \
            --results benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/replay-lab-clean \
            --release-manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/replay-lab-clean/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp/clean-proof" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "Radar agent-lift evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_radar_evidence.py \
            --results benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release \
            --suite-glob 'release-candidate-*' \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --codex-audit-report "$tmp/codex-audit-report.json" \
            --fail-when-no-proof
          check "Radar tool-contract evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_radar_tool_evidence.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/radar-tool/manifest.json \
            --repo-root . \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "workspace Radar evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_workspace_radar_evidence.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/workspace-radar/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "current-repo distill performance evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_distill_perf.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/distill-perf/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "large-repo distill performance evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_distill_perf.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/distill-perf-large/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp/distill-large" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "facts eval evidence" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_facts_eval.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/facts-eval/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          check "release matrix" \
            python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/audit_release_matrix.py \
            --manifest benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release-matrix/manifest.json \
            --out-dir "$tmp" \
            --fail-on-flags
          for report in codex-audit-report.json codex-audit-report.md; do
            compare "release evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          for report in codex-audit-report.json codex-audit-report.md; do
            compare "clean replay-lab proof" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/replay-lab-clean/$report" "$tmp/clean-proof/$report"
          done
          for report in radar-tool-audit-report.json radar-tool-audit-report.md; do
            compare "Radar tool evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/radar-tool/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          for report in workspace-radar-audit-report.json workspace-radar-audit-report.md; do
            compare "workspace Radar evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/workspace-radar/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          for report in distill-perf-audit-report.json distill-perf-audit-report.md; do
            compare "distill performance evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/distill-perf/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          for report in distill-perf-audit-report.json distill-perf-audit-report.md; do
            compare "large-repo distill performance evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/distill-perf-large/$report" "$tmp/distill-large/$report"
          done
          for report in facts-eval-audit-report.json facts-eval-audit-report.md; do
            compare "facts eval evidence" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/facts-eval/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          for report in release-matrix-report.json release-matrix-report.md; do
            compare "release matrix" \
              "benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release-matrix/$report" "$tmp/$report"
          done
          if [ "$failures" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$failures release-evidence check(s) failed"
            exit 1
          fi

  benchmark-real-components:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with: { python-version: "3.14" }
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version-file: go.mod }
      - name: Check out the fixed Graph integration dependency
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: entireio/entire-graph
          ref: b7511131319475860a935d2961b2b272429be4c7 # Graph main after PR #361: read-only store contract
          path: .integration-graph
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Build the real preparation components
        run: |
          go build -o "${{ runner.temp }}/entire-brain" ./cmd/entire-brain
          cd .integration-graph
          go build -o "${{ runner.temp }}/entire-graph" ./cmd/entire-graph
      - name: Exercise public benchmark preparation with local provider output
        env:
          ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_REQUIRE_COMPONENTS: "1"
          ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY: ${{ runner.temp }}/entire-brain
          ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_GRAPH_BINARY: ${{ runner.temp }}/entire-graph
        run: python3 -B benchmarks/agent-brain/test_full_brain_integration.py -v

content.thinking:
I realize test.yml already runs a full sharded Windows test pipeline on depot runners for every PR and push to main, plus a phase1-semantic job on windows-latest — so Windows coverage already exists there before I even look at release.yml.

That said, the real gap is release.yml and nightly.yml: they build on ubuntu only and never actually execute the cross-compiled windows/amd64+arm64 binaries, so the released artifacts themselves are never sanity-checked on Windows. The task's premise about "nothing ever runs them" seems to conflate the general test suite (which does run on Windows) with the release-specific binaries (which don't).

Actually I realize test.yml already triggers on v* tag pushes too, which means the full Windows test suite already runs on release tags — so adding another `go test ./...` on windows-latest in release.yml would just be duplicating coverage that already exists at that exact commit. The real gap is still just verifying the actual built artifact runs correctly on Windows, not re-running the test suite.

Also release.yml doesn't actually depend on test.yml passing — a tag push could publish artifacts even if tests fail, since they're independent workflows. That's a separate gating concern worth flagging even if slightly outside the main scope.

I'm leaning toward adding a windows-latest job that downloads the real shipped artifact, unzips it, and runs the sanity script against it, rather than duplicating the full sharded test suite — but the task explicitly calls for build + go test + sanity, so I need to decide whether to follow it literally or adapt given the overlap with test.yml. This feels like a genuine scope question worth surfacing rather than quietly deciding myself.

The brain branch key is "windows-ci-release-gate" with no stored memories, which is odd since git status showed branch st-georges-v1 — Conductor might rename branches in the background, so I should verify the actual current branch before digging further. Let me go read the README and releasing.md now.

1	# Windows race-test sharding
2	
3	Adapted from entire-graph PR #189, source revision
4	`fbec112800199d918a6e9f9a2c0e98ffc591dfa7`. This port retains Brain's race
5	detector and default pure-Go SQLite backend; it does not enable the `brain_cgo`
6	or `sqlite_fts5` build tags. `CGO_ENABLED=1` supports Go's race runtime.
7	
8	The `test` workflow compiles `internal/cli` once with
9	`go test -race -covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./... -c`, checks the executable's
10	Go build information for race and coverage instrumentation, inventories
11	its runnable Test, Example, and Fuzz roots, and partitions them across eight
12	standard ephemeral Windows runners. Benchmarks are excluded. All remaining
13	Windows packages run once with `go test -race`; native Windows vet runs once
14	separately because direct test binaries bypass go test's automatic vet.
15	The existing cross-build matrix remains in place.
16	
17	The final `test (windows-latest)` check retains the previous required-check
18	name and fails if any prepare, shard, non-heavy, vet, or verification job
19	fails or is skipped. The verifier checks exact root coverage, package/process
20	multiplicity, exit codes, race evidence, binary hashes, toolchain and commit
21	identity, and command-line limits. It requires all planned roots to run and
22	terminate successfully (including legitimate skips), and rejects duplicates
23	and omissions. The compiled inventory is authoritative for newly added tests.
24	
25	The same shard processes also collect atomic, cross-package statement coverage.
26	Each invocation writes a separate profile with its path and SHA-256 bound into
27	execution metadata; the non-heavy package run writes one additional profile.
28	The non-heavy job also runs the instrumented CLI metadata/error contracts once
29	with `tools/coverage/run.py --race --binary-only`, without a second suite run.
30	After validating all execution evidence, the verifier checks profile hashes,
31	format, containment and matching build identity, then unions covered source
32	blocks into `summary.json` and `combined.out`. Missing or corrupt coverage fails
33	verification. The aggregate job renders HTML and publishes the
34	`coverage-windows-sharded` artifact. No separate full-suite coverage job remains.
35	
36	`settings.json` is the tuning surface. The timeout remains 20 minutes per
37	package, shuffle remains off, and Go's default parallelism is preserved.
38	`historical-weights.json` intentionally starts empty: graph timings are not
39	Brain measurements. The deterministic planner initially balances root counts;
40	future weights should come from top-level terminal Elapsed values in retained,
41	successfully verified Brain Windows shard JSONL, recording the source commit
42	and run. No Brain speedup is claimed until native CI has been measured.
43	
44	Every runner restores setup-go's module/build caches. The test-result cache
45	is cleared before execution to ensure tests actually run. Direct launches
46	set PWD to the package directory, prepend GOTOOLDIR to PATH, and preserve
47	`-test.paniconexit0`. The harness inventories target-selected TestMain
48	functions and rejects lifecycle drift until the settings are reviewed.
49	The CLI's pinned `TestMain` isolates XDG storage in a fresh temporary directory
50	for each process, runs `m.Run()` once, and propagates its exit code. It does not
51	filter tests or share state between shards; inventory-only launches also clean
52	up their temporary roots.
53	Before and after execution it verifies the tracked worktree and commit.
54	
55	The separate `phase1-semantic` matrix retains its original race-test command,
56	`ENTIRE_BRAIN_PHASE1_CI=1`, and offline GOPROXY/GOSUMDB environment after module
57	priming. The Linux/macOS race and specialized CGO lanes are unchanged.
58	
59	Validate locally:
60	
61	```sh
62	python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
63	```
64	
65	`prepare.py`, `run_shard.py`, and `run_other.py` require native Windows;
66	the planner, verifier, and harness regression tests run on any host with Go
67	and Python 3.12+. GitHub Actions retains the compiled bundle and all execution
68	and verification evidence for three days. Hosted Actions execution and
69	queue-inclusive latency still require a workflow run.
70	
71	## Native Windows validation
72	
73	The September 6, 2026 Azure VM run passed with Go 1.26.2 and Python 3.12.10:
74	27 harness tests, all eight shards, the remaining package suite, Windows vet,
75	and the coverage/integrity verifier. The CLI inventory accounted for all
76	1,718 roots: 1,700 passed and 18 skipped under existing platform, capability,
77	or opt-in guards. The verifier covered 12 packages in total.
78	
79	The run took 813.527 seconds excluding bootstrap on a four-core
80	`Standard_D4s_v5` VM, with two shards running concurrently in isolated
81	worktrees. This validates native execution; it does not measure the latency
82	of eight separate hosted runners. The separate Phase 1 matrix was not rerun.
83	
84	See [the evidence manifest](evidence/2026-09-06/manifest.json),
85	[execution results](evidence/2026-09-06/execution.json), and
86	[coverage verification](evidence/2026-09-06/verification.json). The manifest
87	binds the tested workflow and harness files to the immutable source snapshot.

# Windows race-test sharding

Adapted from entire-graph PR #189, source revision
`fbec112800199d918a6e9f9a2c0e98ffc591dfa7`. This port retains Brain's race
detector and default pure-Go SQLite backend; it does not enable the `brain_cgo`
or `sqlite_fts5` build tags. `CGO_ENABLED=1` supports Go's race runtime.

The `test` workflow compiles `internal/cli` once with
`go test -race -covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./... -c`, checks the executable's
Go build information for race and coverage instrumentation, inventories
its runnable Test, Example, and Fuzz roots, and partitions them across eight
standard ephemeral Windows runners. Benchmarks are excluded. All remaining
Windows packages run once with `go test -race`; native Windows vet runs once
separately because direct test binaries bypass go test's automatic vet.
The existing cross-build matrix remains in place.

The final `test (windows-latest)` check retains the previous required-check
name and fails if any prepare, shard, non-heavy, vet, or verification job
fails or is skipped. The verifier checks exact root coverage, package/process
multiplicity, exit codes, race evidence, binary hashes, toolchain and commit
identity, and command-line limits. It requires all planned roots to run and
terminate successfully (including legitimate skips), and rejects duplicates
and omissions. The compiled inventory is authoritative for newly added tests.

The same shard processes also collect atomic, cross-package statement coverage.
Each invocation writes a separate profile with its path and SHA-256 bound into
execution metadata; the non-heavy package run writes one additional profile.
The non-heavy job also runs the instrumented CLI metadata/error contracts once
with `tools/coverage/run.py --race --binary-only`, without a second suite run.
After validating all execution evidence, the verifier checks profile hashes,
format, containment and matching build identity, then unions covered source
blocks into `summary.json` and `combined.out`. Missing or corrupt coverage fails
verification. The aggregate job renders HTML and publishes the
`coverage-windows-sharded` artifact. No separate full-suite coverage job remains.

`settings.json` is the tuning surface. The timeout remains 20 minutes per
package, shuffle remains off, and Go's default parallelism is preserved.
`historical-weights.json` intentionally starts empty: graph timings are not
Brain measurements. The deterministic planner initially balances root counts;
future weights should come from top-level terminal Elapsed values in retained,
successfully verified Brain Windows shard JSONL, recording the source commit
and run. No Brain speedup is claimed until native CI has been measured.

Every runner restores setup-go's module/build caches. The test-result cache
is cleared before execution to ensure tests actually run. Direct launches
set PWD to the package directory, prepend GOTOOLDIR to PATH, and preserve
`-test.paniconexit0`. The harness inventories target-selected TestMain
functions and rejects lifecycle drift until the settings are reviewed.
The CLI's pinned `TestMain` isolates XDG storage in a fresh temporary directory
for each process, runs `m.Run()` once, and propagates its exit code. It does not
filter tests or share state between shards; inventory-only launches also clean
up their temporary roots.
Before and after execution it verifies the tracked worktree and commit.

The separate `phase1-semantic` matrix retains its original race-test command,
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_PHASE1_CI=1`, and offline GOPROXY/GOSUMDB environment after module
priming. The Linux/macOS race and specialized CGO lanes are unchanged.

Validate locally:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

`prepare.py`, `run_shard.py`, and `run_other.py` require native Windows;
the planner, verifier, and harness regression tests run on any host with Go
and Python 3.12+. GitHub Actions retains the compiled bundle and all execution
and verification evidence for three days. Hosted Actions execution and
queue-inclusive latency still require a workflow run.

## Native Windows validation

The September 6, 2026 Azure VM run passed with Go 1.26.2 and Python 3.12.10:
27 harness tests, all eight shards, the remaining package suite, Windows vet,
and the coverage/integrity verifier. The CLI inventory accounted for all
1,718 roots: 1,700 passed and 18 skipped under existing platform, capability,
or opt-in guards. The verifier covered 12 packages in total.

The run took 813.527 seconds excluding bootstrap on a four-core
`Standard_D4s_v5` VM, with two shards running concurrently in isolated
worktrees. This validates native execution; it does not measure the latency
of eight separate hosted runners. The separate Phase 1 matrix was not rerun.

See [the evidence manifest](evidence/2026-09-06/manifest.json),
[execution results](evidence/2026-09-06/execution.json), and
[coverage verification](evidence/2026-09-06/verification.json). The manifest
binds the tested workflow and harness files to the immutable source snapshot.

# Releasing Brain

Brain releases the same way Graph does: a tag triggers a build of every target,
the binaries and their checksums are attached to a GitHub release, and a nightly
prerelease is cut from `main` each morning.

## Cutting a release

1. Move the work into a `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, dated.
2. Tag and push:

   ```sh
   git tag vX.Y.Z
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest: it builds `linux`, `darwin`, and
`windows` for both `amd64` and `arm64`, packages each as a `.tar.gz` (`.zip` on
Windows), writes `checksums.txt`, and creates the release with generated notes.
Re-running it against an existing tag updates that release rather than failing.

You can also run it from the Actions tab with a version, which is the way to
re-cut a release whose upload failed.

name: release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release (e.g. v0.1.0). Defaults to the pushed tag."
        required: false
        type: string
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# A tag push and a nightly dispatch can target the same version. Serialize them
# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.
concurrency:
  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.
  group: release-${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo
      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.
      - name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          else
            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          fi
          # A version reaches tag names, file names and release titles. Pin its
          # shape rather than trusting whatever was dispatched.
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to build an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            echo "==> $goos/$goarch"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: build
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          fi
          [[ -n "$version" ]] || { echo "no version to publish" >&2; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)

        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: build
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"

            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

name: nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC daily, matching entire-graph
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Only cut a nightly when main actually moved. A dated prerelease per day that
  # nothing changed is noise, and it makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to
  # answer, not easier.
  changed:
    name: has main moved
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    outputs:
      should_release: ${{ steps.check.outputs.should_release }}
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          base="$(grep -oE '^## +\[?v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null \
                    | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
          [[ "$base" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || base="0.1.0"
          version="v${base}-nightly.$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M).${sha}"

          # Skip when the newest prerelease already points at this commit.
          latest="$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --limit 1 \
                     --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [[ "$latest" == *".${sha}" ]]; then
            echo "main has not moved since $latest — skipping"
            echo "should_release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "should_release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    name: nightly build
    needs: changed
    if: needs.changed.outputs.should_release == 'true'
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.changed.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bare="${VERSION#v}"
          mkdir -p dist
          for t in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"; [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${bare}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${bare}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)

      - name: Publish the prerelease
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.changed.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          gh release create "$VERSION" "${assets[@]}" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --title "$VERSION" \
            --prerelease \
            --generate-notes

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Releasing Brain

Brain releases the same way Graph does: a tag triggers a build of every target,
the binaries and their checksums are attached to a GitHub release, and a nightly
prerelease is cut from `main` each morning.

## Cutting a release

1. Move the work into a `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, dated.
2. Tag and push:

   ```sh
   git tag vX.Y.Z
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest: it builds `linux`, `darwin`, and
`windows` for both `amd64` and `arm64`, packages each as a `.tar.gz` (`.zip` on
Windows), writes `checksums.txt`, and creates the release with generated notes.
Re-running it against an existing tag updates that release rather than failing.

You can also run it from the Actions tab with a version, which is the way to
re-cut a release whose upload failed.

### Why one runner builds everything

Brain's default build is pure Go — both the SQLite driver and the vector path
have cgo-free implementations (`internal/cli/sqlite_driver_purego.go`,
`internal/cli/embed_vec_purego.go`), and SQLite itself comes from
`modernc.org/sqlite` rather than a C binding — so `CGO_ENABLED=0`
cross-compiles every target from one Linux runner.
Graph needs a runner per OS because its tree-sitter bindings need cgo. The
release workflow asserts this rather than assuming it:

```yaml
- name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
  run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
```

If someone adds a cgo dependency to the default build, that step fails and the
release stops, instead of silently producing binaries that only run on the
build host.

The `brain_cgo` build tag still exists for the native embedder. It is not part
of a release build.

## Nightlies

`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs at 06:00 UTC, matching Graph, and tags
`vX.Y.Z-nightly.<timestamp>.<sha>` where `X.Y.Z` is the newest version in the
changelog.

It skips days `main` has not moved. A dated prerelease that is byte-identical to
yesterday's makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to answer, not easier, so
the run checks whether the newest prerelease already points at `HEAD` and exits
if it does.

## Pull requests build the release path

`release.yml` also runs on pull requests that change it. That run builds every
target and skips the publish job, so a change to the release process is proven
on the PR rather than on the tag that depends on it.

## What may be claimed in release material

`mise run release:readiness` reports which claims the retained evidence
supports. It classifies every track as one of `proven`, `local-gated`,
`pending-retained-proof`, `pending-target-evidence`, or `no-claim`, and the gate
fails when release material asserts something the evidence does not carry.

Run it before writing an announcement, and treat anything short of `proven` as
not sayable.

## Install channels

Releases reach users three ways:

| channel | resolves through |
|---|---|
| `entire plugin install brain` | the [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) |
| `scripts/get-brain.sh` | the GitHub releases API, verifying `checksums.txt` |
| a downloaded archive | the release page |

The installer verifies the downloaded archive against `checksums.txt` and exits
non-zero on a mismatch. A missing checksum file is a warning; a wrong checksum
is fatal.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "Gate nightly and release publishing on a Windows verification job" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

The stable-release v0.2.0 gate requires verified Windows artifacts. The release path cross-compiles windows/amd64+arm64 binaries from one Linux runner and nothing ever executed them. The premise needs one correction: `test.yml` already runs the full Go test suite on Windows on every PR, main push, and tag (the sharded `test (windows-latest)` harness) — but it runs with `CGO_ENABLED=1` because the race detector needs cgo. The pure-Go configuration that actually ships (modernc sqlite + purego vector path) was tested nowhere, on any OS, and no shipped binary was ever run.

## What changed

- `release.yml`: new `verify windows` job on `windows-latest`.
